questions.question: Gautam’s present age is equal to 20% of his father's age 15 years ago, and Gaurav's (brother of Gautam) present age is 60% of his father’s age 10 years ago. If the sum of Gautam’s present age and Gaurav’s present age is 31, then find their father’s present age.
questions.questionHtml: Gautam’s present age is equal to 20% of his father's age 15 years ago, and Gaurav's (brother of Gautam) present age is 60% of his father’s age 10 years ago. If the sum of Gautam’s present age and Gaurav’s present age is 31, then find their father’s present age.
questions.solution:
Let the father's present age be X years.

Father's age 15 years ago = (X - 15) years

Gautam's present age = 20% of (X - 15) = \({\\{(X - 15)} \over 5}\) years

Gaurav's present age = 60% of (X - 10) = \({\\{3(X - 10)} \over 5}\) years

\({\\{(X - 15)} \over 5}\) + \({\\{3(X - 10)} \over 5}\) = 31

X - 15 + 3X - 30 = 155

 4X - 45 = 155

4X = 200

X = 50 years

Fatehr's present age is 50 years.

Hence, "option 2" is the correct answer.

questions.question: The market price of an article is Rs. 2720. If a shopkeeper sold the article at 15% loss after giving 25% discount, then the cost price (in Rs.) of the article is:
questions.questionHtml: The market price of an article is Rs. 2720. If a shopkeeper sold the article at 15% loss after giving 25% discount, then the cost price (in Rs.) of the article is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the direct ratio formula between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP):

CP : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 − Loss%)

CP : 2720 = (100 − 25) : (100 − 15) = 75 : 85 = 15 : 17

Since 17 units = 2720, then 1 unit = 2720 ÷ 17 = 160

Cost Price (CP) = 15 × 160 = 2400

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2400.

Alternate Method

Given:

Marked Price (MP) = Rs. 2720

Discount = 25%

Loss = 15%

Step 1: Calculate the Selling Price (SP)

⇒ SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) / 100

⇒ SP = 2720 × (100 − 25) / 100

⇒ SP = 2720 × (75 / 100)

⇒ SP = 2720 × (3 / 4)

⇒ SP = 680 × 3 = Rs. 2040

Step 2: Calculate the Cost Price (CP)

⇒ CP = SP × 100 / (100 − Loss%)

⇒ CP = 2040 × 100 / (100 − 15)

⇒ CP = 2040 × 100 / 85

⇒ CP = 2040 × 20 / 17

⇒ CP = 120 × 20 = Rs. 2400

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2400.

Additional Information

Relation between CP and MP

The relationship is given by CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 ± P/L%), where D is discount, P is profit, and L is loss.

Markup Percentage

Markup % = (Marked Price − Cost Price) ÷ Cost Price × 100.

Effective Discount

For successive discounts d1 and d2, the single equivalent discount is d1 + d2 − (d1 × d2) / 100.

questions.question: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral such that AB is the diameter of the circle and ∠ADC = 145°, then what is the measure of ∠BAC?

Given:

ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral with AB is the diameter of the circle

∠ADC = 145° 

Calculation:

∠ADC + ∠ABC = 180° ...(since the sum of the opposite angles of a quadrilateral is 180°)

⇒ ∠ABC = 180° – 145° 

⇒ ∠ABC = 35° 

Also, ∠ACB = 90°..... (since the angle subtended by diameter at the circumference of the circle, is 90°)

In ΔABC, we have

∠ACB = 90° and ∠ABC = 35° 

So, ∠CAB = 180° – (∠ACB + ∠ABC)

⇒ 180° – (90° + 35°)

⇒ 180° – 125° 

⇒ 55° 

∴ The measure of ∠BAC is 55°

questions.question: If (x + y) 3 + 27(x - y) 3 = (Ax - 2y)(Bx 2 + Cxy + 13y 2 ), then the value of A - B - C is:
questions.questionHtml: If (x + y)<sup>3 </sup>+ 27(x - y)<sup>3</sup> = (Ax - 2y)(Bx<sup>2</sup> + Cxy + 13y<sup>2</sup>), then the value of A - B - C is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Compare the expression with a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2) where a = (x + y) and b = 3(x − y).

First factor: (a + b) = (x + y) + 3(x − y) = 4x − 2y ⇒ Comparing with (Ax − 2y), A = 4.

Second factor: (a2 − ab + b2) = (x + y)2 − 3(x2 − y2) + 9(x − y)2.

Coefficient of x2: 1 − 3 + 9 = 7 (B) | Coefficient of xy: 2 + 0 − 18 = −16 (C).

Calculate: A − B − C = 4 − 7 − (−16) = −3 + 16 = 13.

∴ The correct answer is 13.

Alternate Method

Given: (x + y)3 + 27(x − y)3 = (Ax − 2y)(Bx2 + Cxy + 13y2)

Formula Used: a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2)

Rewrite the left-hand side:

⇒ (x + y)3 + [3(x − y)]3

⇒ [(x + y) + 3(x − y)] [(x + y)2 − (x + y)(3(x − y)) + (3(x − y))2]

⇒ [x + y + 3x − 3y] [(x2 + 2xy + y2) − 3(x2 − y2) + 9(x2 − 2xy + y2)]

⇒ [4x − 2y] [x2 + 2xy + y2 − 3x2 + 3y2 + 9x2 − 18xy + 9y2]

⇒ (4x − 2y) [7x2 − 16xy + 13y2]

Comparing this with (Ax − 2y)(Bx2 + Cxy + 13y2):

⇒ A = 4, B = 7, C = −16

Calculating the required value:

⇒ A − B − C = 4 − 7 − (−16)

⇒ −3 + 16

⇒ 13

∴ The correct answer is 13.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identities

Standard factorization of sum and difference of cubes: a3 ± b3 = (a ± b)(a2 ∓ ab + b2).

Expansion Formulas

(a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2 and (a − b)2 = a2 − 2ab + b2.

Comparison of Coefficients

If two polynomials are equal for all values of variables, the coefficients of their corresponding terms must be identical.

Quantity = 25 kg

Profit = SP – CP

Profit%= (Profit/CP) × 100

⇒ 900

⇒ 1250

questions.question: What is the difference in the mean proportional between 1.8 and 3.2 and the third proportional to 5 and 3?
questions.questionHtml: What is the difference in the mean proportional between 1.8 and 3.2 and the third proportional to 5 and 3?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Mean Proportional (M) = √(1.8 × 3.2) = √(5.76) = 2.4

Third Proportional (T) = 32 ÷ 5 = 9 ÷ 5 = 1.8

Difference = 2.4 − 1.8 = 0.6

∴ The correct answer is 0.6.

Alternate Method

Given: First set (1.8, 3.2) for Mean Proportional; Second set (5, 3) for Third Proportional.

Formula Used:

1. Mean Proportional of a and b = √(a × b)

2. Third Proportional of a and b = b2 / a

Calculations:

⇒ Mean proportional (M) = √(1.8 × 3.2)

⇒ M = √(18/10 × 32/10) = √(576/100) = 24/10 = 2.4

⇒ Third proportional (T) = (3 × 3) / 5

⇒ T = 9 / 5 = 1.8

⇒ Difference = M − T = 2.4 − 1.8 = 0.6

∴ The correct answer is 0.6.

Additional Information

Mean Proportional

It is the middle term of a geometric progression. If x is the mean proportional between a and b, then a:x = x:b, which gives x = √(ab).

Third Proportional

If c is the third proportional to a and b, then the ratio a:b = b:c, which simplifies to c = b2/a.

Fourth Proportional

If d is the fourth proportional to a, b, and c, then a:b = c:d, implying d = (b × c)/a.

questions.question: There are two water taps in a tank which can fill the empty tank in 12 hours and 18 hours respectively. It is seen that there is a leakage point at the bottom of the tank which can empty the completely filled tank in 36 hours. If both the water taps are opened at the same time to fill the empty tank and leakage point was repaired after 1 hour, then in how much time the empty tank will be completely filled?
questions.questionHtml: There are two water taps in a tank which can fill the empty tank in 12 hours and 18 hours respectively. It is seen that there is a leakage point at the bottom of the tank which can empty the completely filled tank in 36 hours. If both the water taps are opened at the same time to fill the empty tank and leakage point was repaired after 1 hour, then in how much time the empty tank will be completely filled?
questions.solution:
Given:

Time taken by first water tap to fill the empty tank = 12 hours

Time taken by second water tap to fill the empty tank = 18 hours

Time taken by leakage to empty the filled tank = 36 hours

Formula used:

Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation:

LCM of 12, 18 and 36 is 36

Efficiency of first water tap = 36/12 = 3 units/hr

Efficiency of second water tap = 36/18 = 2 units/hr

Efficiency of leakage = 36/36 = 1 unit/hr

Efficiency of these 2 taps and leakage together = (3 + 2 – 1) = 4 units/hr

Remaining units = (36 – 4) = 32 units

Work done by two tap water together to fill the empty tank = 32/(3 + 2) hr

⇒ 32/5 hr

⇒ 6.4 hours = 6 hours + 0.4 hours (0.4 hours = 24 minutes)

⇒ 6 hr 24 min

Total time taken to fill the empty tank = (6 hr 24 min + 1 hr)

⇒ 7 hr 24 min

∴ The empty tank will completely filled in 7 hr 24 minutes

Shortcut Trick

For the first one hour = (3 + 2 - 1) × 1 = 4 units

Time to fill remaning tank = (36 - 4) ÷ (3 + 2) = 6.4 hours

Total time taken = (6.4 + 1) = 7.4 hours = 7 hr 24 min

∴ The empty tank will completely filled in 7 hr 24 minutes

Now,

⇒ tanθ – cotθ =  [1- (√3 + 1)2]/(√3 + 1)

questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
 
A. These kinds of sharks are known as obligate ram ventilators because they draw water in through their mouths and force it out through their gills.
B. They use a method called buccal pumping, in which water is pulled in through the mouth and forced out through the gills by the cheek muscles.
C. It is true that many types of sharks must keep moving in order to receive life-giving oxygen from the water passing through their gills.
D. Other types of sharks are able to remain stationary because they possess special structures called spiracles, which force water out through their gills.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is CABD.
 

Key Points 

  • Sentence C tells us about the main idea of the paragraph i.e. sharks move in order to receive life-giving oxygen from the water through their gills.
  • Sentence A continues that the sharks that draw water in through their mouth and force it out through their gills are called obligate ram ventilators.
  • Followed by sentence A, sentence B continues as it tells us that process of drawing water in through the mouth and forcing it out through the gills is called Buccal pumping.
  • Sentence D, concludes by telling that other sharks remain stationary as they have spiracles (a special structure to force water out through their gills). 
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
So the correct passage is- (C) It is true that many types of sharks must keep moving in order to receive life-giving oxygen from the water passing through their gills. (A) These kinds of sharks are known as obligate ram ventilators because they draw water in through their mouths and force it out through their gills. (B) They use a method called buccal pumping, in which water is pulled in through the mouth and forced out through the gills by the cheek muscles. (D) Other types of sharks are able to remain stationary because they possess special structures called spiracles, which force water out through their gills.

Hinglish 

  • वाक्य C हमें पैराग्राफ के मुख्य विचार के बारे में बताता है यानी शार्क अपने गलफड़ों के माध्यम से पानी से जीवनदायिनी ऑक्सीजन प्राप्त करने के लिए चलती हैं।
  • वाक्य A जारी रखता है कि शार्क जो अपने मुंह से पानी खींचती हैं और अपने गलफड़ों के माध्यम से उसे बाहर निकालती हैं, उन्हें ओब्लिगेट रैम वेंटिलेटर कहा जाता है।
  • वाक्य A के बाद वाक्य B जारी है क्योंकि यह हमें बताता है कि मुंह के माध्यम से पानी खींचने और इसे गलफड़ों के माध्यम से बाहर निकालने की प्रक्रिया को बुक्कल पंपिंग कहा जाता है।
  • वाक्य D, यह कहकर समाप्त होता है कि अन्य शार्क स्थिर रहती हैं क्योंकि उनके पास स्पाइरैकल होते हैं (उनके गलफड़ों के माध्यम से पानी को बाहर निकालने के लिए एक विशेष संरचना)।
  • इसलिए, सही उत्तर विकल्प 2 है।
